title: KV-prefetch + routing scratchpad (Aaron Cole)
content:
Context:
- Personal scratchpad for thinking through a combined KV-prefetch + routing feature to reduce tail latency and token cost for common interactive workloads (chat, conversational search).
- Cross-team notes: running experiments with static prefix caching and predictive prefetch; need to align with product-hosted-api and serving-runtime teams.

Problem statement:
- Many customer workloads have high reuse of short prefix tokens (system prompts, instructions, recent turns). Cold KV cache misses are a major contributor to early-token latency and redundant compute.
- Current serving runtime uses on-demand KV caching. This is simple but leads to:
  - first-request tail latency (50-95ms extra per early token on some model/hardware combos)
  - extra GPU cycles when many concurrent sessions cause repeated recomputation of identical prefixes
  - poor SLOs for low-latency tiers and higher cost for bursty traffic

Goals (measurable):
- Reduce median first-token latency by ~10-25ms for 0-4 token responses across targeted workloads.
- Reduce per-session token cost for high-reuse prefixes by 5-15% (dependent on workload).
- Avoid increasing overall GPU memory pressure beyond safe limits for Dedicated customers.

High-level ideas / approaches:
1) Static prefix prefetching
   - Allow customers to register immutable prefixes (system messages, instruction templates) at model-route level. Prefetch KV cache into an LRU with TTL on model instance warmup.
   - Config: prefix list, prefetch_on_startup boolean, ttl_seconds, min_free_kv_ratio
   - Pros: predictable, low complexity, easy to audit for PII; good for PLG users with templates
   - Cons: requires explicit config; doesn't help ad-hoc dynamic prefixes

2) Predictive prefetch (heuristic / ML)
   - Observe recent user sessions and surface N most-likely next-prefixes. Prefetch based on session signals: user-agent, route, prompt fingerprint, time-of-day.
   - We can start with simple heuristics: top-k per-route prefixes by frequency; then add lightweight model to predict next-prefix probability.
   - Risk: privacy considerations (avoid prefetching user PII), increased complexity

3) Session-local adaptive prefetching
   - When a user starts a session, prefetch the most-likely continuation of their conversation based on the first turn. Keep small per-session cache with eviction.
   - Useful for multi-turn chat where the first system prompt implies a standard follow-up (e.g., "Summarize this..." -> prefetch summarization prefix)

4) Routing integration: route to warmed instances
   - Smart routing policies that prefer instances with warm KV for a given prefix set. Fallback to cold instances if capacity constrained.
   - Routing metadata: prefix-fingerprint -> instance warmness score. Use shard-level advertising of which prefixes are loaded.

API / config sketch (route-level):
- prefetch: { enabled: true/false, mode: static|heuristic|session, prefixes: ["..."], ttl: 3600, max_cached_prefixes: 64 }
- routing_policies: { prefer_warm_instances: true, warmness_threshold: 0.7 }
(note: use JSON/YAML in real PRD)

User stories:
- As an app engineer, I want to declare my system prompt as a route-level prefix so that my app's first-response latency is predictable. Acceptance: route-level config deploys, first-response p50 improves by target.
- As a platform engineer, I want routing to prefer instances that already have my route's registered prefixes to avoid cold-cache misses. Acceptance: traffic skew to warm instances measured; fallback works.
- As a privacy officer, I want a way to opt-out certain routes from predictive prefetching and to ensure logged prefixes are scrubbed. Acceptance: opt-out flag respected; logs scrub PII patterns.

Experiment plan (MVP):
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): Static prefix only
  - Implement route-level static prefix list + startup prefetch on Dedicated and Hosted (low-risk).
  - Short experiment on a subset of PLG routes (50 routes) to measure latency/cost delta.

- Phase 2 (4 weeks): Heuristic top-k per-route
  - Compute top-k prefixes from route history in analytics; prefetch top-3 on startup.
  - Add metric collection: warm_hit_rate, first_token_latency, extra_memory_used.

- Phase 3 (6-8 weeks): Routing warmness integration + session prefetch prototypes
  - Route preference API + instance warmness advertising via control-plane.
  - Canary for customers on Dedicated.

Metrics to track:
- first_token_latency_p50/p90/p95 for targeted routes
- kv_cache_hit_rate (new metric reflecting prefetched vs on-demand)
- gpu_cycles_saved_per_prefix (estimate)
- memory_evictions_per_minute (safety signal)
- rollback_count / customer impact incidents

Risks & mitigations:
- Memory pressure: limit max_cached_prefixes per instance and implement min_free_kv_ratio; prefer eviction over OOM.
- Privacy: static prefixes ok; block predictive on routes flagged as sensitive; provide scrubber + opt-out.
- Complexity: start with static and heuristic before ML predictor. Keep observability hooks.

Open questions / parking lot:
- What is the canonical representation of a "prefix" across model variants and quantization formats? (fingerprint similarity?)
- How to measure cost savings accurately across batching effects? (need offline sim)
- UX for customers to manage prefix lists at scale (UI/CLI/SDK?)
- Should we expose metrics for warmness per-instance to tenants? (leak risk)
- Interplay with KV compression / shared prefix deduping across routes

Immediate TODOs (for next week):
- Sync with product-hosted-api (Priya) to validate route config surface (owned by product).
- Spike: 1-day prototype that injects static prefix into a single GPU instance startup and measures first-token latency delta. (Owner: Aaron)
- Create Confluence draft (link above) and attach sample telemetry dashboards.
- File JIRA tickets: INF-342 (static-prefetch MVP), INF-343 (heuristic collection job), INF-344 (routing warmness API)

Notes to self:
- Keep initial API conservative: explicit opt-in for PLG; default off for Dedicated except selectable via account admin.
- Talk to SRE about autoscaler interaction: heavy prefetching on scale-up could cause spike in memory usage. Throttle prefetching rate on node startup.

References & links:
- prior scratchpads: llm-prefetch-kv-cache-scratchpad.json, llm-prefetch-prd-scratchpad-aisha-khan.json
- infra PR: /pull/1287 (serving-runtime prefetch proto)

End of scratchpad.

-- Aaron
